A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRB framework and CRUCB algorithm. All 33 pages of v3 and 38 pages of v4, including proofs, experimental appendices, tables, and figures, support comparison. Retained content can be matched across reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic combinatorial-bandit experiments and AntMaze reinforcement-learning results, including regret curves and exploration heatmaps in Section 6 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v4 retains original synthetic and AntMaze results, updates the AntMaze curves, and adds original window-parameter sensitivity results in Appendix F.4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the post-initialization loop from t = 1,...,T to t = 2K+1,...,T, correcting the stated accounting for initialization rounds. The Future-UCB estimator and combinatorial Solver remain unchanged; expanded window-size explanations do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same shortest-path, AntMaze, k-MAX, matching, and spanning-tree tasks, including their retained difficulty variants. The new sensitivity study uses existing Path-easy coverage. LLM-based planning is only a proposed application.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain R-ed-UCB, SW-UCB, SW-TS, SW-CUCB, and SW-CTS in corresponding benchmark comparisons. SW-CUCB's inclusion in the revised main-text Figure 8 reuses a comparison already present in v3 Appendix G.

E3.justification: Appendix F.4 introduces a Path-easy evaluation sweeping epsilon over 0.05, 0.125, 0.25, and 0.4, measuring regret at 100K, 200K, and 300K episodes. Existing task specifications and AntMaze settings in Tables 1–2 are retained. The newly disclosed main-experiment epsilon does not establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: v4 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing whether CRUCB's cumulative regret depends on its window-size parameter. The revised Figure 8 redisplays existing Appendix G heatmaps rather than introducing a new robustness experiment or case study.

E5.justification: Figure 7 changes the reported AntMaze aggregation from three runs to five while retaining 99% confidence intervals. The PDFs do not explicitly establish whether this reflects additional runs or corrected reporting. New Table 3 provides no run count or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Both AntMaze regret curves and their uncertainty regions in Figure 7 are updated alongside the revised reported run count. Table 3 adds twelve sensitivity results; at 300K episodes, regret ranges from 19060.71 to 19061.90 across epsilon values. The existing synthetic benchmark curves are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 changes an intermediate ratio's denominator from the reward of pi'_const in v3 Equation 48 to that of pi*_const in v4 Equation 47. Section 2 also makes the bounded-mean condition explicit. The principal theorems, regret bounds, and proof constructions remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the CRB formulation, CRUCB algorithm, near-matching regret bounds, and empirical effectiveness in synthetic and deep-RL settings. v4 emphasizes practical impact more strongly, but does not materially change these contributions or their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explanation of SW-CUCB's repeated attempts at impossible AntMaze edges, interprets the new sensitivity results as parameter robustness, and proposes LLM-based planning as another application. The qualifications concerning non-concave AntMaze outcomes and fixed action structures are retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link and explicitly reports epsilon = 0.125 for the main experiments. Section 4 expands documentation of the proportional window and interchangeable optimization oracle. Existing AntMaze implementation details and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v4 updates application references, including replacing Hyperband with Huang et al. (2021) for automatic machine learning. Appendices A–B add chain-of-thought, progressive-hint prompting, and Amichay and Mansour (2025). The central positioning against existing rising and graph-triggered bandits remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises the abstract, introductory framing, problem-formulation prose, and conclusion, and adds explanations of epsilon, Solver, and the analytical parameter q. The title becomes plural, author/conference information changes, and acknowledgments and an LLM-writing disclosure are added. The main section sequence and proof organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adopts conference formatting, enlarges and relocates Figure 6, and replaces Figure 8 with selected edge-level heatmaps already in Appendix G. Figure 3 is redrawn to show the existing 2/3 upper and 1/2 lower exponent floors. Table 3 is added; most other displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility documentation through the stated main window parameter and code-access link, adds direct sensitivity evidence, and corrects Figure 3 to reflect the already-stated regret bounds. These are useful, limited gains. The sensitivity evidence covers only Path-easy and lacks uncertainty information, while the central method, benchmark coverage, and theoretical results remain largely intact.
